terminal.description: A shell in your workspace. Run the waiting list here, and try your methods from main.

tasks.title: Make the waiting list
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 1` in `WaitingList.java`, write a method called `waitingList`. It takes a `String[]` of the people in the queue, in order, and an `int`, the seats on the boat. The first `seats` people in the queue board; it gives back a new `ArrayList<String>` of everyone after them, in queue order.

Check calls `waitingList` with queues and boats of its own, one where everyone gets a seat, and reads every name on the list it gives back.
nextSteps: Write the first line: the method gives back an `ArrayList<String>`.
Make a new, empty list inside the method.
Loop over the queue from the first person without a seat to the end, adding each one.
Give the list back, and print it from `main`.
hints: `new ArrayList<>()` makes an empty list; `add` puts a name at its end.
The first `seats` people are at positions 0 to `seats - 1`. The first one without a seat is at position `seats`.
Inside: `ArrayList<String> waiting = new ArrayList<>();`, then `for (int i = seats; i < queue.length; i++) { waiting.add(queue[i]); }`, then `return waiting;`.

videos.title: Adding, reading and removing in an ArrayList

tasks.title: Find the last name on the list
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 2`, write a method called `lastOnList`. It takes an `ArrayList<String>` and gives back a `String`: the last name on it, or `Nobody` when the list is empty. It only reads the list: the list stays as it was.

Check calls `lastOnList` with lists of its own, an empty one included, and reads what it gives back and the list afterwards.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about reading a list: it has no square brackets and no `length`.
Work out the position of the last name from the list's size.
Try it from `main` with the waiting list, then with an empty list.
hints: A list tells you how many names it holds with `size()`, and gives the name at a position with `get`.
Positions start at 0, so the last is one less than the size. An empty list has no last position at all.
The shape is `if (waiting.size() == 0) { return "Nobody"; }` then `return waiting.get(waiting.size() - 1);`.

tasks.title: Keep the loads of the crossings that sailed
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 3`, write a method called `sailedLoads`. It takes an `int[]` of passengers, one per crossing, and gives back a new `ArrayList<Integer>` of the counts above 0, in order. Walk the array with a for-each loop.

Check calls `sailedLoads` with arrays of its own, an empty one included, reads every number on the list it gives back, and reads your lines for the for-each loop.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about lists of numbers and the word `Integer`.
Write the first line and make an empty list of whole numbers.
Walk the array with a for-each loop, and add each count above 0.
Give the list back, and print it from `main`.
hints: A list holds objects, so a list of whole numbers is written `ArrayList<Integer>`, never `ArrayList<int>`. Adding an `int` to it just works.
The for-each loop over an array reads `for (int count : passengers)`: each time round, `count` is the next value.
Inside the loop: `if (count > 0) { loads.add(count); }`, with `ArrayList<Integer> loads = new ArrayList<>();` before it.

tasks.title: Cancel every booking under a name
tasks.description:
Under `// Task 4`, write a `void` method called `cancel`. It takes an `ArrayList<String>` of bookings and a `String`, a name, and removes every booking under that name from the list it was given. The other bookings stay, in their order.

Check makes lists of its own, one with two bookings under the name side by side, calls `cancel` on each, and then reads the list it passed in.
nextSteps: Read the part of the lesson about removing from a list while you walk it.
Decide which way to walk the list so that removing does not make you step over a name.
Compare each booking with the name using `equals`, and remove it when they match.
Try it from `main`: the bookings list there has the same name twice.
hints: `remove(i)` takes out the item at position `i`, and every item after it moves one place forward.
Walking from the end to the start, the items that move have already been looked at. A for-each loop cannot remove at all.
Loop `for (int i = bookings.size() - 1; i >= 0; i--)`, and inside write `if (bookings.get(i).equals(name)) { bookings.remove(i); }`.
